27b625f81c8a00e8.title: My Chemical Romance The Black Parade 2026
27b625f81c8a00e8.desc: Formed in Newark, NJ, My Chemical Romance made its debut in 2002 with the independently released album I Brought You My Bullets, You Brought Me Your Love. The band signed to Reprise Records the following year and made its major label debut with 2004’s Three Cheers for Sweet Revenge, now 3x certified Platinum. The album contained the Platinum hit "I'm Not Okay (I Promise)," the Gold-certified "Helena," and "The Ghost of You." Rolling Stone hailed their third studio album, The Black Parade (3x Platinum) as one of the top albums of 2006. Lead single “Welcome to the Black Parade” topped both Billboard’s Alternative Songs chart and the UK’s Official Singles chart and is now 3x Platinum. The band toured extensively behind the album – appearing as characters from The Black Parade – and released the live album The Black Parade is Dead! in 2008. Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys was released in 2010 and topped Billboard’s Alternative Albums and Top Rock Albums charts. It was followed by a series of singles which as a whole made up the Conventional Weapons release in 2013. My Chemical Romance’s songs continue to rack up half a billion global streams each year.

2705bb5c1df030e5.title: Malcolm Todd: Do That Again Tour
2705bb5c1df030e5.desc: When Malcolm Todd graduated high school in 2022, he told his parents he would be taking a gap year to pursue music. They, unsurprisingly, were less than thrilled by the proclamation, but gave him a year to see if it could work. They learned what the rest of the music industry quickly realized: never bet against Malcolm Todd. “Every single day since I told my mom I wanted to do this, I have actively worked to grow my fanbase, to get better at music, to build this world,” he explains. By the time he shared Sweet Boy in 2024, his day job at Cold Stone was in the rearview. Tracks like “Roommates” were racking up millions of streams daily. Fast forward a year, and Todd is more motivated than ever on his self-titled album, a declaration that he isn’t a hype machine or a flash in the pan, but a generation-defining voice. That ambition is immediate on “Bleed,” the first single from Malcolm Todd. It features Omar Apollo, who serves as the lone guest on the album. Buoyed by a bouncy bassline, crisp drums, and an intoxicating synth melody, Malcolm and his frequent collaborators Jonah Cochran and Charlie Ziman, tried to make something as poppy as they possibly could. With most of the album…

270e48c30891dcaa.title: The Bad Plus
270e48c30891dcaa.desc: This is the farewell tour of The Bad Plus — the last chance to see them live. For over two decades, The Bad Plus have been one of the most influential and distinctive formations in modern jazz. The American band came to international attention in the early 2000s and quickly built a reputation for opening jazz to new audiences with complete musical conviction — uncompromising, stylistically open, and full of enormous energy. The group became famous for their radical reinterpretations of rock and pop songs as well as for their original compositions. Over the course of their career, The Bad Plus released numerous acclaimed albums on labels including Columbia Records and Nonesuch, and collaborated with artists such as Joshua Redman, Wendy Lewis, and Bill Frisell. 2026 marks the end of an era: the band has announced they will dissolve after their current tour. That makes this an especially rare opportunity to experience one of the defining groups of modern jazz one final time. Between complex structures, improvisational openness and enormous rhythmic precision, The Bad Plus have left a lasting mark on the sound of contemporary jazz.

27f02fd1db540e03.title: Divorce Care Higher Vision Church
27f02fd1db540e03.desc: No matter how amiable, separation or divorce is one of the most painful experiences. But you are not alone: there is a DivorceCare support group for people walking through separation or divorce. DivorceCare is a safe, welcoming place where people understand the difficult emotions and challenges of separation and divorce. Over 13 weeks, you’ll find relief and comfort as you learn what to expect in the days ahead and how to navigate your personal healing journey. Since separation and divorce can be messy and confusing, you’ll learn helpful ways of coping with the challenges and navigating relationships—and gain solid support each step of the way. Topics include how to manage divorce-related emotions such as loneliness, anxiety, bitterness, anger, and grief; how to cope with the changes in your life and relationships; the importance of forgiveness; and how to navigate legal and financial issues. At a weekly DivorceCare meeting, you will view a video featuring respected counselors, teachers, and healthcare professionals on divorce and recovery topics.
